item.title: Street Fighter 5 celebrates 10th anniversary today with a history of its unfinished launch to a long road of redemption
item.description: <p>Street Fighter may find itself in a really good place right now (for the most part), but that wasn't the case a decade ago.</p> <p>Today marks the 10th anniversary of <a href="https://www.eventhubs.com/moves/sf5/">Street Fighter 5</a>'s launch, which is going to bring up a lot of complicated feelings among the fighting game community, though its history of initial mistakes led to a long road to redemption.</p>

item.title: The first true mirror match in Street Fighter history was due to a bug and could only be played against the CPU
item.description: <p>The first Street Fighter (sometimes called "Fighting Street") was originally released back in 1987. It was mostly a single player fighting game that saw its user controlling Ryu against Adon, Birdie, Eagle, Geki, Gen, Joe, Lee, Mike, Retsu and Sagat.</p> <p>It was possible for some multiplayer action. Players could choose between Ryu and Ken, though they operated exactly the same. For all intents and purposes, this was just a mirror match.</p>

item.title: Dead or Alive 6: Last Round will not include Mai Shiranui and Kula Diamond nor crossplay or upgrades for existing owners
item.description: <p>There had been rumblings that Dead or Alive was not as dead as it seemed until recently, and that turned out to be correct.</p> <p>Koei Tecmo <a href="https://www.eventhubs.com/news/2026/feb/12/new-dead-alive-announce/">announced Dead or Alive 6: Last Round as well as a new Dead or Alive project</a> last week, and now we have a better idea as to what is and is not included in the upgraded title.</p>
